examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}が{町|まち}の{安全|あんぜん}を{守|まも}っている。
examples.english: The police are protecting the safety of the town.

examples.japanese: この{法律|ほうりつ}は{子|こ}どもの{権利|けんり}を{守|まも}るために{作|つく}られた。
examples.english: This law was created to protect children's rights.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}をきちんと{守|まも}る{人|ひと}は{信頼|しんらい}される。
examples.english: People who strictly keep to their scheduled times are trusted.

examples.japanese: {交通|こうつう}ルールを{守|まも}らないと、{事故|じこ}を{起|お}こす{危険|きけん}がある。
examples.english: If you don't follow traffic rules, there's a risk of causing an accident.

notes:
{守|まも}る has two main meanings: to protect and to follow/obey.

TRANSITIVITY:
Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)

MEANING 1 (PROTECT):
- {家族|かぞく}を{守|まも}る: to protect one's family
- {国|くに}を{守|まも}る: to defend the country
- {身|み}を{守|まも}る: to protect oneself

MEANING 2 (OBEY/FOLLOW):
- ルールを{守|まも}る: to follow rules
- {約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}る: to keep a promise
- {時間|じかん}を{守|まも}る: to be punctual
- マナーを{守|まも}る: to observe manners

OPPOSITE:
- {攻|せ}める: to attack (vs. protect)
